text:
Within one human day are all the days
+
+of time, from that inconceivable
+
+first day of time, when a terrible
+
+God preordained the days and agonies,
+
+until that other day when the ubiquitous river
+
+of earthly time returns to its source,
+
+which is Eternity, and present,
+
+future, yesterday, and what is now mine go dark.
+
+Between dawn and night lies universal
+
+history: From night I see
+
+at my feet the pathways of the Hebrew,
+
+Carthage annihilated, Hell and Glory.
+
+Give me, Lord, courage and joy
+
+to scale the summit of this day.

translation.title: James Joyce
translation.editorial_note: One day contains sacred and universal history in a Joycean compression; the final prayer turns the cosmic scheme into the human labor of enduring a day.
